fake_success_scan: MigrationStepResult has no PASS state a step can claim without its underlying real operation succeeding: Apply's PASS branch is reached only after run_upgrade() returns without raising against a real SQLAlchemy/Alembic call; Verify re-reads applied_revision and PRAGMA integrity_check from the real target rather than trusting the Apply step's own claim; Rollback Point's PASS is reached only through RecoveryService.prove_by_restore, which performs a real restore into a scratch file and calls the caller's verifier - the identical no-file-copy-alone discipline Phase 5 established for BACKUP_VERIFIED. migration_impact.analyze_file never executes a migration file (ast.parse only, matching migrations.py's own contract_of discipline), so impact analysis cannot itself mutate a database. check_migration_data_loss_risk is re-derived over the live docs/alembic/versions/ directory on every call, never read from a report's own claim - proven by test_step_3/test_step_4 in the journey and, negatively, by TestKnownDataLossRiskBlocksTheWholeSequence's synthetic destructive fixture.

limitations: No PostgreSQL migration evidence: no PostgreSQL driver is installed on this host (verified directly - ModuleNotFoundError for both psycopg2 and psycopg), so PostgreSQL-specific migration/apply behaviour is honestly NOT_CONFIGURED, not fabricated; ADR-0006 registers the engine-neutral abstraction as MANDATORY and verified PostgreSQL operation as explicitly not a canonical requirement, unchanged by this phase. No Stable-revision rollback is claimed or implemented: Rollback Point here is Phase 5's proven-backup lineage, hardened, not ROLLBACK_STABLE - that stays Phase 22B (Recovery Supervisor), and pdp.py::_rollback_rule is untouched. No production HTTP or UI surface exposes MigrationSafetySequence; it is a library composition only, matching every other Phase-20-adjacent authority's own scope boundary. The impact analyser's data-loss-risk detection is deliberately conservative (op.drop_table, op.drop_column, and a raw destructive op.execute) - it does not attempt to infer risk from op.alter_column narrowing (e.g. nullable=False) without a prior-schema comparison, which would require guessing rather than deriving.
blockers: Matrix Gate column HUMAN_GATE_6 ("APPLY of a migration to real or stable data") maps to the whole of Phase 20 in GovernanceState.phase_gates (mechanical matrix-cell derivation - the identical mechanism Phase 19's HUMAN_GATE_4 used) and is not recorded ACCEPTED in docs/acceptance/HUMAN_GATE_RECORDS.md as of this submission (still "not reached", verified directly). GovernanceState/PhaseGateChecker.check_human_gate will therefore return BLOCKED and the verdict AWAITING_HUMAN_GATE, regardless of every other check's result. This is a genuine, mechanically-derived stop condition, not a defect in this candidate, and it cannot be self-granted by an implementing actor - only the human acceptance authority may record an HGR-00N granting it. No BLOCKER/HIGH finding is open. Phase 5 and Phase 6 (this phase's prerequisites) are both MACHINE-ACCEPTED. This is the first Phase 20 submission, so no re-scoring authority is applicable.
